name: Chest Tummy Time
howTo: Place baby face-down on your bare chest at a 45° recline. Get face-to-face — your face is their strongest motivation to lift their head.
materials: A reclined chair, couch, or pillows to prop yourself up

name: Floor Tummy Time
howTo: Lay baby face-down on a firm, clean surface. Place a rolled muslin under chest to ease the lift. Start 2 min and add 1 min per week.

name: Bicycle Legs
howTo: Lay baby on back; hold ankles gently and move legs in slow cycling motions. Say 'pedal, pedal' rhythmically while maintaining eye contact.

name: Arm Stretch & Midline
howTo: Gently hold baby's forearms, slowly extend arms outward, then bring hands together at midline over chest. Repeat 5 times each side.

name: Visual Tracking Card
howTo: Hold a high-contrast B&W card 25 cm from baby's face. Move it slowly left then right. Let eyes find it before you move again.

name: Supported Upright Hold
howTo: Hold baby upright against your shoulder and let them practice holding their head for 10–15 seconds. Support gently — don't grip.

name: Leg Kicking Scarf
howTo: Hold a light scarf 15 cm above baby's feet while they lie on back. Let them discover kicking makes it move — first cause-effect feedback.

name: Side-Lying Practice
howTo: Place baby on their side with a rolled towel tucked behind their back for support. Alternate sides each session; 5 min per side.

name: Finger Grasp Reflex
howTo: Place your index finger in baby's palm and let the grasp reflex close around it. Gently tug to stimulate the grip.

name: Palm Massage
howTo: With warm hands make small circular motions across each palm and each finger. Open fisted hands gently with thumb-stroke wrist to fingertips.

name: Hand Opening Stroke
howTo: When baby's fists are clenched, gently stroke from wrist to fingertips along the back of the hand to encourage opening.

name: Arm-to-Midline Assist
howTo: Gently bring baby's hands together at the centre of their chest. Hold 3 seconds, release. This builds bilateral brain coordination.

name: Wrist Rotation
howTo: Hold baby's forearm steady and gently rotate the wrist in small circles, 5 times each direction on each hand.

name: Soft Object in Palm
howTo: Place a small rolled cloth in baby's palm. Note how long the grasp reflex holds it and whether they bring it toward their mouth.

name: Narrate Every Routine
howTo: Talk through every nappy change, feed, and bath. 'Now I'm lifting your legs. This might feel cool.' Tone matters more than words.

name: Daily Lori / Song
howTo: Sing one consistent song at the same time each day. Repetition builds a neural safety pattern. Same song, same voice, every day.

name: Vowel Mirroring
howTo: When baby makes any vowel sound, mirror it back exactly. Pause 10 full seconds before speaking again — that gap is the lesson.

name: Serve and Return Pause
howTo: After speaking or making a sound, count to 10 silently before responding again. You are teaching conversation structure.

name: Name Recognition Distance
howTo: Call baby's name from 1 metre away (not from directly in front). Watch for eyes or head turning toward the sound.

name: Sound Exploration
howTo: Introduce one new household sound daily: wooden spoon on pot, rustling paper, running water. Watch how baby stills and locates.

name: Parentese Talk
howTo: Use a slightly higher pitch and slower pace than normal when talking to baby. This is biologically optimal for infant language processing.

name: Read Aloud (Any Text)
howTo: Read any book, recipe, or message aloud to baby. The vocabulary range and rhythm matter — comprehension is irrelevant at this stage.

name: High-Contrast Cards
howTo: Hold a black-and-white card 25 cm from baby's face. Let them fixate 10 seconds before moving slowly left. Newborn vision peaks at this distance.

name: Face Gazing
howTo: Hold your face 20–30 cm from baby's. Make one slow exaggerated expression and hold it. Wait 10 seconds for their response.

name: Mirror Gazing
howTo: Hold a small unbreakable mirror 25 cm from baby. They won't recognise themselves yet — but the responsive face is deeply engaging.

name: Disappearing Face Peek
howTo: Cover your face with your hands. Hold 3 seconds. Reveal warmly. Very early object permanence and social anticipation practice.

name: Light and Shadow
howTo: Carry baby toward a window or lamp. Let them observe light change as you move closer and further. Narrate: 'Bright! Now darker.'

name: B&W Pattern Book
howTo: Hold a high-contrast picture book 25 cm from baby. Spend 20–30 seconds on each page before turning. One page can hold attention this age.

name: Skin-to-Skin Hold
howTo: Undress baby to nappy and hold against bare chest tummy-to-tummy. Cover both lightly. Regulates temperature, cortisol, and heart rate.

name: Smile Mirroring
howTo: When baby makes a mouth movement or social smile, reflect it back immediately and wait. You are teaching: my expression has social power.

name: Responsive Holding
howTo: When baby cries, respond before escalation. Consistent early response builds the secure attachment base for all future relationships.

name: Emotional Narration
howTo: Name what you see: 'You look uncomfortable. Let me see what's wrong.' Labelling emotional states builds the circuits for self-regulation later.

name: Caregiver Rotation
howTo: Let each main caregiver hold baby skin-to-skin. Each person's unique warmth and heartbeat is a distinct and valuable regulatory experience.

name: Calm Modelling
howTo: When you feel anxious, slow your own breathing while holding baby. They sense and entrain to your nervous system state.

name: Tel Maalish (Oil Massage)
howTo: Warm oil in palms. Begin with legs — least sensitive. Long slow strokes hip to foot, then arms, back, head. Stimulates vagus nerve.

name: Texture Touch Exploration
howTo: Gently touch different textures to baby's palm and feet: soft cloth, smooth wood, cool spoon. Name each: 'Soft. Smooth. Cool.'

name: Outdoor Air & Light
howTo: Take baby outside for 10–15 min. Wind, natural light, birdsong, and temperature variation are multi-sensory inputs no indoor space can replicate.

name: Water Temperature Play
howTo: During bath, pour water at slightly different temperatures on hands. Narrate: 'Warm water now. A little cooler.'

name: Chest Hum Vibration
howTo: Place baby against your chest and hum or sing. The physical vibration is felt across their whole body and is deeply calming.

name: Hunger Cue Recognition
howTo: Learn early hunger cues: rooting, hand-to-mouth, stirring. Feed before crying. Responding to early cues builds baby's signal-response trust.

name: Wake Window Awareness
howTo: Track awake time: 0–6 weeks = 45–60 min; 6–12 weeks = 60–90 min. Beginning sleep routine before overtiredness sets in improves settling.

name: Tummy Time + Toy
howTo: Place an interesting toy just out of reach during tummy time. The motivation to lift and reach makes effort more sustained.

name: Rolling Facilitation
howTo: In tummy time, gently rock baby's hips toward one side. Give the nervous system the sensation of weight transfer needed for rolling.

name: Floor Roll Practice
howTo: Place baby on their back. Gently cross one leg over the other and let momentum encourage rolling to the side. Celebrate any attempt.

name: Supported Sitting (Lap)
howTo: Sit baby on your lap facing outward, hands loosely around their trunk. Let them feel the work — don't over-support.

name: Forearm Weight Bearing
howTo: In tummy time, once baby pushes up on forearms, gently rock their hips side to side. This is the direct predecessor of rolling.

name: Leg Press Against Hands
howTo: Hold your palms against baby's feet while they lie on back. Let them push — this activates leg extensors used later for standing.

name: Bounce on Lap
howTo: Hold baby upright on your lap, supporting under arms, and let them bounce slightly. Vestibular input and leg strength combined.

name: Tummy Time Mirror
howTo: Prop an unbreakable mirror in front of baby during tummy time. Their own face is one of the strongest motivators to lift the head.

name: Reach for Hanging Object
howTo: Hang a lightweight object (cloth, spoon) just above baby's chest while they lie on back. Wait — let them discover swiping makes it move.
materials: Cloth, ribbon, or spoon on string

name: Two-Handed Grasp
howTo: Offer a toy wider than one hand. Watch whether they use both hands together — bilateral integration milestone appearing around 4–5 months.

name: Object Transfer Observation
howTo: Give a toy in one hand, then offer a second near the other. Do they transfer the first, or hold both? Transfer appears around 5–6 months.

name: Shake and Listen
howTo: Hand baby a small container with dried lentils inside. Let them discover shaking makes sound — first voluntary cause-effect action.

name: Crinkle Paper Explore
howTo: Give a piece of crinkled paper or foil (supervised). The sound, texture, and visual feedback engage three senses simultaneously.

name: Palm Pressure Exploration
howTo: Press a textured surface gently against baby's palm — a mesh bag, rough towel, smooth cup. The hand's sensory map is being built now.

name: Babble Echo Session
howTo: When baby coos or babbles, echo it back exactly. Then add one new syllable: 'ooh… and then… ba?' Pause 10 seconds each time.

name: Laugh Trigger Search
howTo: Try raspberry sounds, sudden peekaboo, lifting gently in the air. The belly laugh — appearing around 3–4 months — is a major milestone.

name: Consonant Introduction
howTo: Model ba-ba-ba, ma-ma-ma, da-da-da during alert windows. These are the first consonants baby will produce at 5–6 months.

name: Two-Language Narration
howTo: Speak in two languages fluidly during routines. 'Now we're washing your hands — haath dho rahe hain.' Bilingual input from birth is a gift.

name: Name-to-Face Link
howTo: Point to each family member and say their name slowly. 'This is Dadi. Dadi.' Repetition over weeks builds face-name recognition.

name: Music Variety Session
howTo: Play a different musical genre each day this week — classical, folk, jazz, film songs. Varied sound builds auditory discrimination.

name: Respond to Name — Moving
howTo: Call baby's name from different positions: behind, left, right. Turn-to-name appearing consistently by 6 months is a key milestone.

name: Pause in Song
howTo: Sing a familiar song and stop mid-verse. Wait. Watch baby's face — anticipation appearing means they have learned the pattern.

name: Object Permanence Level 1
howTo: While baby watches, slowly hide your face behind a cloth or book. Wait 5 seconds. Reveal. Object permanence for faces is appearing now.

name: Cause-Effect Toy
howTo: Give baby a rattle. Let them discover that shaking = sound. When they look surprised after shaking, they have understood cause-effect.
materials: Rattle or sealed container with lentils

name: Container In-and-Out
howTo: Show baby how to put an object into a bowl and take it out. Let them try. In-out schema is foundational for spatial reasoning.

name: Look-Where-I-Point
howTo: Point at objects and then look at baby's face — do they follow your point? Joint attention developing around 5–6 months.

name: Texture Comparison
howTo: Give two very different textures simultaneously — smooth and rough. Let baby feel both and switch between them. Comparison is the lesson.

name: Anticipatory Game
howTo: Do an action three times that baby enjoys — a raspberry, a bounce. On the fourth, pause before. Watch for anticipatory smile.

name: Social Smile Response
howTo: Every time baby smiles, reflect it back immediately with warmth. Teaching: my positive emotion has social power. This builds communication.

name: Stranger Presence Practice
howTo: When a new person is present, hold baby and engage the person warmly yourself. Baby reads your calm as: this person is safe.

name: Protest Response
howTo: When baby shows displeasure at a game stopping, restart it. Teaching: expressing a feeling produces a response. Foundation of communication.

name: Separation Practice
howTo: Step out of baby's visual field for 30 seconds. Return before they cry. Gradually extend. Teaching: the person comes back.

name: Emotional Vocabulary
howTo: Name emotions you see: 'You love that sound! Your face lit up.' Accurate emotional labelling builds the brain's emotional vocabulary.

name: Joint Attention Object
howTo: Hold up an interesting object and look between it and baby's face — object, baby, object. This is joint attention, a language precursor.

name: Water Kicking (Bath)
howTo: Let baby kick freely in the bath for 5 extra minutes. Water resistance builds leg strength while providing rich sensory feedback.

name: Sensory Walk (Held)
howTo: Walk outside slowly, narrating each sensory experience: 'That's wind on your face. Listen — that's a crow.' Multi-sensory saturation.

name: Varied Food Textures (Intro)
howTo: If starting solids, introduce one very smooth purée at a time. Oral sensory exploration — taste and texture together — is its own skill.

name: Dance and Sway
howTo: Hold baby and sway or dance to music with rhythm. Vestibular input plus auditory rhythm is two systems activating simultaneously.

name: Temperature Contrast Hands
howTo: Alternate placing a cool and slightly warm cloth against baby's hands. Narrate each change. Temperature discrimination is developing.

name: Feeding Cue Ritual
howTo: Establish a consistent pre-feed sequence (dim lights, hold position, a specific phrase). Predictability regulates baby's anticipatory state.

name: Nap Cue Sequence
howTo: Same 3–4 steps before every nap: swaddle/sleep sack, darken room, white noise, feed. Consistent cues train the brain to prepare for sleep.

name: Sitting Balance Challenge
howTo: Sit baby on firm surface. Place a toy slightly to the side so they must lean to reach. Each topple-and-catch is a core strength exercise.

name: Crawling Encouragement
howTo: Place a desirable toy 50 cm in front of baby on the floor. Stay beside or behind — not in front — so they crawl away from you.

name: All-Fours Rocking
howTo: Place baby on hands and knees (support if needed). Place a toy just out of reach. Watch for rocking — the crawl motor pattern loading.

name: Obstacle Crawl
howTo: Place a rolled blanket or sofa cushion in the crawl path. Watch whether baby navigates around or over it. Motor problem-solving.

name: Pull to Stand (Assisted)
howTo: Position baby next to a stable low piece of furniture. Place a toy on the surface above their head. Support at hips, not hands.

name: Pivot in Tummy Time
howTo: Place a toy at 45° from baby in tummy time. Watch them pivot their body to follow. This uses the same muscles as crawling.

name: Walking Hold (Two Hands)
howTo: Hold both of baby's hands from behind and let them walk forward at their own pace. Alternate to one hand as confidence grows.

name: Stair Climbing (Supervised)
howTo: Let baby crawl up 2–3 safe stairs with you directly behind. Stair climbing builds strength, coordination, and spatial awareness.

name: Pincer Grasp Practice
howTo: Place large puffed snacks or safe small objects on a tray. Watch how they pick up — raking grasp transitioning to pincer grasp.
materials: Puffed snack or small safe object

name: Object In Container
howTo: Give a large container and 4–5 objects. Let baby drop them in and dump them out repeatedly. Foundational spatial reasoning.

name: Banging Objects Together
howTo: Give two objects and demonstrate banging them together. When baby copies, bilateral motor coordination and cause-effect are both working.

name: Page Turning (Board Book)
howTo: Offer a board book and let baby try to turn pages. Even clumsy turning is fine motor skill and book engagement combined.

name: Stack and Topple
howTo: Stack 2 blocks, let baby knock them over. The knock is as developmental as the build — cause-effect with a satisfying outcome.

name: Transfer Between Containers
howTo: Show baby how to move an object from one bowl to another. This requires spatial planning and goal-directed motor action.

name: Canonical Babbling Echo
howTo: When baby produces ba-ba, da-da, or ma-ma, echo immediately and expand: 'Ba ba ba! And then — da da da?' Pause 10 seconds.

name: Respond to Name (Consistent)
howTo: Test: call baby's name from 2 m away in a normal voice. Consistent response by 9 months is a key language milestone.

name: Gesture Introduction (Wave)
howTo: Wave goodbye every single time anyone leaves. Every time, consistently. First gestural communication appears 8–10 months.

name: Point and Name
howTo: Point at objects throughout the day and name them. When baby points at something, immediately name it and comment.

name: Book Naming Session
howTo: Board book: point to each picture, name it, wait 5 seconds. 'Woh kya hai? Haan — aam! Mango. Peela aam.' Dual-language counts.

name: Simple Instruction Practice
howTo: Use consistent simple instructions with gesture: 'Come here' + open arms. 'Give me' + open hand. Gesture + word together.

name: Babble Conversation Record
howTo: Record 2 minutes of serve-and-return babble conversation. Listen back — count how many turns baby takes. Target: 3+ by 9 months.

name: Name Body Parts (Touch)
howTo: Touch each body part and name it while bathing or dressing. 'Yeh naak hai. Yeh haath.' Touch plus name = dual encoding.

name: Object Permanence (Under Cloth)
howTo: Show baby an interesting toy. While they watch, hide it under a cloth. Say 'Kahaan gayi?' Watch whether they search under the cloth.

name: Means-Ends: Pull Cloth
howTo: Place a toy on a cloth, toy out of reach but cloth within reach. Watch if baby pulls the cloth to get the toy — means-ends planning.

name: Cause-Effect: Button Toy
howTo: Any toy that produces a response when pressed or moved. Systematic testing of what each element does is emerging scientific method.

name: Simple Sorting (Big/Small)
howTo: Offer objects in two distinct sizes. Watch how baby handles them differently — size discrimination precedes sorting by months.

name: Imitation Game
howTo: Tap a surface, shake your head, clap — do a simple action and wait. Imitation of familiar actions appears around 8–9 months.

name: Memory Game (Where Did It Go?)
howTo: Let baby see you hide an object under one of two cups. Which cup do they look under? Tracking invisible displacement is developing.

name: Stranger Anxiety Support
howTo: When baby shows anxiety with new people, hold them securely and engage the stranger warmly. Don't force contact — baby reads your calm.

name: Protest Honour
howTo: When baby clearly communicates 'no more' (turns away, arches), stop immediately. Teaching: your communication is respected.

name: Separation Practice Extended
howTo: Leave baby with a known caregiver for 10–15 min. Return before distress. Consistent returns build the trust that makes separations easier.

name: Mirror Play Together
howTo: Sit in front of a large mirror with baby. Point to their reflection, then yours. 'Kaun hai yeh? Tum ho!' Social-cognitive learning.

name: Laugh Trigger Catalogue
howTo: Find 3 things that reliably make baby laugh. Do them daily. The belly laugh is a major social-emotional development marker.

name: Object Permanence — People
howTo: Call 'Where's Papa?' when Papa is out of sight. Watch baby look toward the right location. Person permanence = secure attachment working.

name: Textured Surface Crawling
howTo: Let baby crawl on different surfaces: carpet, smooth floor, grass, a mat outside. Each surface is different proprioceptive input.

name: Water Play (Supervised)
howTo: Extended bath time — 15 min. Let baby splash, pour, and explore. Water provides resistance, temperature, visual, and auditory input simultaneously.

name: Nature Texture Explore
howTo: Outdoors: let baby touch bark, leaves, stones, soil (if safe). Natural textures are the richest sensory input available.

name: Mouth Exploration (Safe Objects)
howTo: At this age, mouthing is the primary sensory tool. Provide safe, clean objects of varied size and texture. Don't interrupt unless unsafe.
materials: Safe household objects of varied texture

name: Sound Localisation Game
howTo: Make an interesting sound from behind baby, left, right, and above. Watch how accurately they turn toward each direction.

name: Spoon Introduction
howTo: Give baby a spoon during feeding. Messy self-feeding attempts — however unsuccessful — build fine motor and self-care simultaneously.

name: Cup Introduction
howTo: Offer a small open cup with a tiny amount of water. Supervised sipping — not for intake, for the skill of cup management.

name: Cruising Along Furniture
howTo: Place a toy at the far end of the sofa. Baby learns to step sideways while holding on — each step is a walking lesson.

name: First Steps Between Points
howTo: Sit 1–2 steps from furniture baby is holding. Open arms and call their name. Close the gap gradually as confidence grows.

name: Standing Balance Challenge
howTo: While baby stands holding furniture, catch their attention from the other side. Count the independent standing seconds each day.

name: Stair Descent Practice
howTo: With you directly behind, let baby learn to descend stairs backwards (feet first). This is safer than forward and builds spatial awareness.

name: Ball Kicking
howTo: Roll a large soft ball toward baby's feet while they stand with support. Kicking combines balance, timing, and motor planning.

name: Carry While Walking
howTo: Ask baby to carry a lightweight object while walking (holding your hand). Dual-task walking builds automaticity.

name: Push-Along Toy Walk
howTo: Give baby a push-along toy (cardboard box works) to push while walking. The resistance helps them control speed and direction.

name: Rough-Ground Walking
howTo: Walk on grass, gravel path, or slight slope with one hand held. Variable terrain builds adaptive balance faster than smooth floors.

name: Pincer Grasp Refinement
howTo: Offer small safe objects on a tray. A precise thumb-index pincer grip developing by 12 months is a fine motor milestone.

name: Scribble with Crayon
howTo: Hold a crayon with baby's hand and make marks on paper. The first deliberate mark — even if uncontrolled — is the beginning of writing.

name: Stacking 2–3 Blocks
howTo: Demonstrate stacking 2 blocks then hand one to baby. Can they place it on top? 2-block tower by 12 months = spatial milestone.

name: Post into Container (Slot)
howTo: Cut a slot in a box lid and provide objects that fit through. Posting requires visual-spatial matching — demanding for this age.

name: Turn Pages (Board Book)
howTo: Let baby turn board book pages. Even turning multiple at once counts — the intent to turn is the milestone, not the accuracy.

name: Unscrew Lid
howTo: Offer a large-lidded container. Show loosening a lid; let them try. Rotation movements are a distinct fine motor skill.

name: Mama' and 'Dada' with Meaning
howTo: When they say 'mama' or 'dada' directed at the correct person, respond warmly and immediately. First true words are emerging now.

name: First Word Inventory
howTo: This week, note every consistent sound used to mean a specific thing. 'ba' always for ball = a first word even if it doesn't sound adult.

name: Expand Every Utterance
howTo: When baby says one word, add two: 'ba' → 'ball! Big red ball.' Every expansion teaches: what you said has a more complete version.

name: Bye-Bye Gesture (Contextual)
howTo: Wave bye-bye every single time anyone leaves. First spontaneous contextual wave — not prompted — marks true gestural communication.

name: Point + Name Response
howTo: Every time baby points, immediately name what they're pointing at and comment. The point deserves a full response, every time.

name: Follow Simple Instruction
howTo: Come here' / 'Give me' / 'Where is the ball?' with consistent gesture. Following 1-step instructions by 12 months is a key milestone.

name: Nursery Rhymes with Actions
howTo: Sing rhymes with hand actions: 'taalee bajao', 'Johny Johny'. Baby learns to do the actions before saying the words.

name: Name 3 Body Parts
howTo: During bath or dressing, ask 'Kahaan hai naak?' and point. Recognising 2–3 body parts on command by 12 months is typical.

name: Object Permanence (Two Locations)
howTo: Hide a toy under one of two cloths while baby watches. Do they search the correct one? Searching correctly = solid object permanence.

name: Imitate Household Tasks
howTo: Hand baby a cloth when you wipe a surface. Give them a spoon when you stir. They imitate because they understand the action's purpose.

name: Simple Puzzle (2 Pieces)
howTo: A 2-piece puzzle — shape fits a hole — shows visual discrimination, spatial rotation awareness, and persistence.

name: Find Object Under Cup
howTo: Show baby the toy going under one cup. Reverse the cup with the toy and ask: where did it go? Object-tracking in 3D space.

name: Pretend Play Introduction
howTo: Pretend to drink from an empty cup, or put a toy phone to your ear. When baby imitates — symbolic thought has arrived.

name: Problem Solving: Open Box
howTo: Put a favourite toy in a closed (not locked) box. Watch what baby does to open it — persistence and problem-solving combined.

name: Affection Initiation
howTo: Note whether baby initiates affection — reaches up to be held, hugs, brings you objects. These are attachment behaviours to celebrate.

name: Limit Testing Observation
howTo: When baby deliberately drops something and watches your reaction — they are testing social rules. Calm, consistent responses are the lesson.

name: Empathy Seed
howTo: If someone nearby is crying or upset, narrate what you see: 'Woh reh rahi hai. Shayad dukh lag raha hai use.' Early empathy wiring.

name: Short Separation Practice
howTo: Leave for a consistent 15–20 minute trip. Confident goodbye + return as promised + warmth on return = secure separation learning.

name: Play Alongside Another Child
howTo: Arrange play near another baby. No expectation of interaction — parallel play beside another child is the correct stage right now.

name: Social Game Repetition
howTo: Repeat a social game (peek-a-boo, tickle, bounce) and stop mid-way. Watch baby signal for continuation — communication is purposeful.

name: Sensory Bin Introduction
howTo: Fill a shallow container with dry rice or lentils. Let baby scoop, pour, and run hands through. Supervised closely.

name: Outdoor Ground Texture
howTo: Let baby crawl or stand on grass, sand, or mud (if safe). The resistance and texture of outdoor ground is uniquely rich input.

name: Music and Movement
howTo: Hold baby and move to music with a clear beat. Note what genres they respond to — musical personality is forming.

name: Whole-Body Movement Play
howTo: Roll baby gently in a blanket, lift in air briefly, spin slowly. Vestibular system thrives on varied whole-body movement.

name: Messy Play Introduction
howTo: Puréed food or yoghurt on a tray. Let baby touch, smear, and explore. Tactile tolerance built now prevents later sensory avoidance.

name: Spoon Practice Self-Feed
howTo: Baby-led spoon feeding — messy and slow is correct. The independence matters more than the quantity eaten.

name: Shoes and Socks Off
howTo: Let baby try to remove their own socks. This develops fine motor skill and body-care independence simultaneously.

name: Walk on Uneven Ground
howTo: Daily outdoor walking on grass, gravel, or slopes builds adaptive balance far faster than smooth indoor floors.

name: Climbing on Low Furniture
howTo: Let baby climb on and off a sofa cushion on the floor under supervision. Climbing builds shoulder, core, and spatial judgement.

name: Squat to Pick Up
howTo: Place toys on the floor and encourage baby to squat to retrieve them instead of bending at the waist. Squat builds hip and core strength.

name: Kick a Ball Forward
howTo: Roll a large soft ball toward baby and encourage kicking. Timing, balance on one foot, and motor planning combine in this action.

name: Throw a Ball
howTo: Demonstrate overhead throwing and let baby try. Even wild attempts build the shoulder rotation and release control needed for throwing.

name: Walk and Carry
howTo: Ask baby to carry a lightweight object from one room to another. Dual-task locomotion shows walking is becoming automatic.

name: Dance Freely
howTo: Put on music and dance together. Free movement to music builds coordination, rhythm, and body awareness simultaneously.

name: Stair Up and Down
howTo: Practice going up and down stairs with one hand held. By 15 months most children can navigate with support.

name: Crayon Mark Making
howTo: Large crayons on big paper. Any mark is the goal — this is the beginning of all future writing. Celebrate every mark.

name: Stacking 4+ Blocks
howTo: Stack 4 blocks and let baby copy. Knock down and restart. 4-block tower by 15 months is solid fine motor development.

name: Shape Sorter (Circle)
howTo: Start with just the circular hole — no rotation needed. Success with circle before introducing shapes that require rotation.

name: Bead Threading (Large)
howTo: Thread large beads or pasta onto a thick cord. Requires two-hand coordination, visual targeting, and sustained attention.

name: Fill and Pour
howTo: Water play with two containers — fill one, pour into other. The control of pouring is a fine motor skill used in self-care for years.

name: Peel Stickers
howTo: Place large stickers on paper and let baby peel them off. Pinch-peel requires precise finger coordination.

name: 10+ Word Vocabulary
howTo: Count consistent words this week including approximations. Target: 10+ words by 15 months. Each is celebrated explicitly.

name: Two-Word Combination Watch
howTo: Listen for first two-word combinations: 'more doodh', 'mama up'. These typically appear 15–18 months and mark a major leap.

name: Name 5 Body Parts
howTo: Extend body part naming to 5: naak, haath, paon, aankhein, kaan. Can baby point to each when named?

name: Picture Book Naming
howTo: Point to pictures and ask 'What's this?' Wait. If no answer, name it and move on. No pressure — repeated exposure is what builds it.

name: Follow 2-Step Instruction
howTo: Pick up the ball AND put it in the box.' Two-step unrelated instructions mark a significant receptive language leap.

name: Pretend Telephone Call
howTo: Hold a wooden spoon to your ear: 'Hello? Yeh kaun hai?' Let baby take it. Symbolic play and communication combined.

name: Expand + Add More
howTo: When baby says 'ball', say 'ball — red ball — big round ball!' Each expansion teaches vocabulary and sentence structure simultaneously.

name: Sing-and-Fill
howTo: Sing a familiar song and pause before the last word of each line. Wait for baby to fill it in vocally or with gesture.

name: Simple Pretend Sequence
howTo: Baby feeds a doll, puts it to sleep, covers it with a cloth. Three-step pretend = narrative thinking beginning.

name: Match Identical Objects
howTo: Give baby two identical cups and two identical spoons. Can they match the cups together and spoons together?
materials: Two matching pairs of household objects

name: Find Under Two Cups
howTo: Hide a toy under one of two cups while baby watches. Swap the cups slowly. Which cup do they check? A-not-B error is normal now.

name: Sort by Colour (One Colour)
howTo: Place all red objects in one pile, all blue in another — demonstrate. Don't expect success yet; the repeated demonstration is the teaching.

name: Early Number Concepts
howTo: During stacking or sorting, count aloud slowly: 'Ek, do, teen.' One-to-one counting comprehension comes later — hearing it is the start.

name: Cause-Effect Complexity
howTo: Offer a toy with multiple actions: press this to make sound, turn that to see movement. Systematic testing of each element is science.

name: Parallel Play Beside Peer
howTo: Arrange play near another toddler. Don't expect interaction. Parallel play is the developmentally correct stage — don't rush sharing.

name: Tantrums as Communication
howTo: When a tantrum happens, narrate calmly: 'You're very frustrated. You wanted that and you can't have it. That's hard.' Name — don't fix.

name: Mine' Acknowledgement
howTo: When baby says 'mine', acknowledge the feeling: 'Yes, that's yours.' Teaching ownership feelings before teaching sharing.

name: Comfort Object Introduction
howTo: If baby has a preferred toy or cloth, honour it. A comfort object is not a crutch — it is an autonomous self-regulation tool.

name: Proud Moments Response
howTo: When baby achieves something, your response matters. Specific warm praise: 'You put all the blocks in! You worked hard at that.'

name: Independence in Play
howTo: Create a safe floor space and let baby play alone for 5–10 minutes without intervention. Independent play is a skill to build.

name: Messy Sensory Play
howTo: Cooked spaghetti, wet sand, or yoghurt on a tray. Sensory tolerance for unfamiliar textures is built through repeated low-pressure exposure.

name: Nature Walk and Collect
howTo: Walk outdoors and collect leaves, stones, sticks (safe). Back home, handle and sort them. Natural materials are rich sensory input.

name: Rhythm Instruments
howTo: Pots, wooden spoon, dried rice in a container. Make music together. Rhythm production is both sensory and fine motor.

name: Spinning and Rolling
howTo: Roll baby gently on the floor or spin slowly in arms. Vestibular input supports balance, posture, and regulation.

name: Playdough (Atta)
howTo: Knead some atta (wheat dough) together. Baby squeezes, pokes, and flattens. Playdough is pure fine motor and tactile input.

name: Spoon Use Practice
howTo: Encourage spoon use at every meal, however messy. Competence by 18 months is the target — not table manners, just the motor skill.

name: Partial Dressing Help
howTo: Ask baby to push their arm through a sleeve or lift a foot for a sock. Participation — however partial — builds independence.

name: Running Practice
howTo: Running at 16–18 months is stiff-legged but consistent. Give open safe space and let them run freely — don't slow them down.

name: Walk Up Stairs (Rail)
howTo: Walk up stairs holding the rail, one hand held. Alternating feet on stairs typically appears around 2 years — step-together is fine now.

name: Kick Ball with Aim
howTo: Set up a 'goal' (two objects as posts) and encourage kicking the ball between them. Directed kicking requires motor planning.

name: Jump Off Step (Both Feet)
howTo: Stand baby on the bottom stair or a thick book. Encourage jumping off with both feet. Landing with both feet = motor milestone.

name: Climbing Ladder / Slide
howTo: At a playground or safe homemade version, let baby climb up and come down a small slide. Height + movement = vestibular rich.

name: Pedal (Push Along Ride-On)
howTo: A push-along ride-on (or cardboard box to sit in) builds leg strength and spatial navigation before a true pedalling bike.
materials: Ride-on toy or adapted cardboard box

name: Balance Beam Walking
howTo: Make a 'beam' with masking tape on the floor. Encourage walking along the line with arms out. Balance challenges in a safe context.

name: Carry Heavy Load
howTo: Ask baby to carry a small bag with a few books inside across the room. Heavy carrying is regulating to the sensory system.

name: Drawing Lines
howTo: Show drawing a horizontal line across paper and let baby try. Any deliberate directional mark is an achievement.

name: Unscrew and Screw Lids
howTo: Practice opening and closing containers with twist lids. Rotation movements are a distinct fine motor skill used in daily life.

name: Stacking 6+ Blocks
howTo: 6-block tower requires spatial planning, grip calibration, and controlled release. Each additional block is harder than it looks.

name: Tear Paper
howTo: Provide magazines or old newspaper for tearing. Bilateral tearing requires both hands working in opposition — a coordination milestone.

name: String Beads (Large)
howTo: Thread 5 large beads or pasta pieces onto a shoelace. Requires visual targeting, bilateral coordination, and sustained attention.

name: Puzzle (4–6 Piece)
howTo: A simple inset puzzle builds visual discrimination, spatial rotation, and the tolerance for trial-and-error failure.

name: 20–50 Word Vocabulary
howTo: By 18 months, 20–50 words (including approximations) is the developmental target. Under 10 words by 18 months warrants a paediatrician mention.

name: Two-Word Combinations
howTo: More doodh', 'bye dada', 'big ball.' Two-word phrases by 18 months are a major milestone. Model them in all conversation.

name: What's That?' Response
howTo: Baby will point at everything and say 'woh kya hai?' or similar. Every time: name it, describe it in one sentence, wait.

name: Story Telling (Simple)
howTo: Tell a simple 3-sentence story about something that happened today. Story structure — beginning, middle, end — is absorbed before it is produced.

name: Animal Sounds Game
howTo: Kutte kya bolta hai? Bhow bhow!' Sound-to-animal linking builds vocabulary through a different encoding channel.

name: Action Word Focus
howTo: Focus on verbs this week: running, eating, sleeping, jumping. Action vocabulary is as important as noun vocabulary.

name: Reading Together Daily
howTo: Same book, multiple days in a row. When baby anticipates a page, they are demonstrating memory, sequence, and language — simultaneously.

name: Singing Along
howTo: In familiar songs, pause on the last word of each line and wait. By 18 months many babies fill in the word — word retrieval practice.

name: Simple Pretend Cooking
howTo: Give baby pots, spoons, and empty containers. Let them 'cook.' Pretend play now represents real sequences observed in daily life.

name: Sort by Shape (2 Shapes)
howTo: Sort objects into two groups by shape: round things here, flat things there. Demonstrate; don't expect immediate success.

name: Picture-to-Object Match
howTo: Show a picture of a cup, then ask baby to find the real cup. Picture-object correspondence is an abstract cognitive skill.

name: Order Completion
howTo: Begin a familiar routine and stop mid-way. Watch baby signal or try to complete it — sequence memory is confirming itself.

name: Count with Objects
howTo: Place 1, then 2, then 3 objects in a line counting aloud as you do. One-to-one correspondence is being seeded; production comes later.

name: Problem Solving: Unstick
howTo: Tape a desirable toy lightly to a table or box. Watch how baby figures out removing the tape or pulling the object free.

name: Emotion Coaching
howTo: When emotions arise, sit close and name the emotion specifically: 'You're angry. That felt unfair.' Don't fix — just name and stay.

name: Feelings Chart Introduction
howTo: Put a simple 4-face chart on the wall: happy, sad, angry, scared. 'How are you feeling today? Point to the face.' No judgment.

name: Practice Goodbye Ritual
howTo: Develop a 3-step goodbye sequence for separations. Consistent, brief, warm — never long and uncertain. Consistency reduces distress.

name: Cooperative Game (Roll Ball)
howTo: Sit facing each other and roll a ball back and forth. Taking turns in a structured physical game is cooperative play emerging.

name: Show Empathy in Books
howTo: When a character in a book is sad or scared, narrate: 'Woh dara hua hai. Tum kya sochte ho?' Perspective-taking through story.

name: Household Helper
howTo: Let baby 'help' wipe a surface, stir food, hand you objects. Social participation and competence are both being built.

name: Sensory Bin (Varied Fill)
howTo: This month use a different fill each week: sand, water, dried beans, shredded paper. Sensory tolerance broadens with variety.

name: Outdoor Barefoot Walking
howTo: Walking barefoot on grass, sand, or dirt provides proprioceptive richness that shoes remove. 10 minutes barefoot outdoors = rich input.

name: Clay or Dough Play
howTo: Commercial clay or homemade atta dough. Squeezing, rolling, and flattening are pure fine motor with rich tactile feedback.

name: Sound Discrimination
howTo: Make the same sound loudly and quietly — the same instrument or voice. Can baby identify louder and quieter? Auditory discrimination.

name: Blanket Roll and Burrito
howTo: Roll baby gently in a blanket — not tight. The whole-body deep pressure is calming for the nervous system and delights most toddlers.

name: Spoon and Fork Independence
howTo: Offer fork for stabbing soft foods. Fork + spoon both available. Child chooses — autonomy in eating builds a positive food relationship.

name: Washing Hands Routine
howTo: Demonstrate hand washing before every meal and after outdoors. By 18 months, with reminding and help, this is beginning to establish.

name: Running with Direction Changes
howTo: Set up a simple course: run to the tree, run back. Direction change while running requires significant motor planning updates.

name: Jump with Both Feet
howTo: From ground level, encourage jumping with both feet simultaneously leaving the ground. Landing on both feet = major gross motor milestone.

name: Walk Up and Down Stairs (Rail)
howTo: Practice both directions on stairs with one hand on rail. Safety and independence are both being built.

name: Kick Stationary Ball
howTo: Place a ball on the ground and ask baby to kick it. A stationary kick before a rolling ball — motor precision building.

name: Balance on One Foot Briefly
howTo: Hold baby's hand and ask them to lift one foot for 2 seconds. Brief one-foot balance appearing 18–24 months.

name: Climbing Frames
howTo: Any safe climbing frame or jungle gym. Climbing is the most efficient builder of strength, coordination, and risk assessment.

name: Throwing at a Target
howTo: Set up a large container and throw soft balls into it from a metre away. Aimed throwing builds visual-motor coordination.

name: Ride-On and Steer
howTo: Push-along ride-on with steerable wheels, or just steering a cart. Navigation and steering need practice just like walking did.

name: Draw Vertical Line
howTo: Show drawing a line from top to bottom and let toddler try. Directional mark-making is the direct precursor to letter formation.

name: Copy Circle
howTo: Show drawing a circle slowly and let toddler try. Circle before straight lines — fine motor milestone at 24–27 months when it appears.

name: Stack 8+ Blocks
howTo: 8-block tower requires sequential spatial planning: each level must be stable before the next. The planning IS the developmental work.

name: Cut with Child Scissors
howTo: Introduce child-safe scissors with a parent steadying the paper. Cutting requires bilateral coordination and sustained grip.

name: Peg in Pegboard
howTo: Press pegs into a pegboard. Requires visual targeting, push force calibration, and the release of placing.

name: Lace Large Holes
howTo: Lace a shoelace through large holes in cardboard. Pre-lacing builds the same hand movements as actual shoe-lacing later.

name: 50–100 Word Vocabulary
howTo: 50+ words by 20 months is solid. Under 20 consistent words by 20 months is worth discussing with a paediatrician.

name: Three-Word Phrases
howTo: More apple please', 'Mama come here.' Three-word combinations beginning to appear 19–24 months.

name: Refer to Self by Name
howTo: Aryan do it!' Using own name before 'I' is developmentally normal and means self-concept is forming.

name: Ask 'Why?' Game
howTo: When toddler asks 'why' (it starts!), answer simply and then ask 'why do you think?' Turn every why into a conversation.

name: Story Re-tell
howTo: After reading a familiar book, close it and ask 'What happened?' Listen for any sequence — even one event recalled is narrative memory.

name: Colour Naming Focus
howTo: Introduce one colour per week. Label it consistently all week: 'The red cup. Your red shoes. Red tomatoes!' One at a time works best.

name: Follow 2-Step Instruction (Unrelated)
howTo: Pick up the cup AND bring it to me.' Two unrelated steps in sequence tests working memory as well as language.

name: Conversation Practice
howTo: Ask open questions about recent experiences: 'What did you see at the park?' Don't correct answers — expand and continue.

name: Cause-Effect Multi-Step
howTo: Stack 3 books then push — watch toddler's face. Set up a ramp and roll a ball down. Multi-step cause-effect chains are interesting now.

name: Categorise Animals vs Food
howTo: Use pictures or objects: sort animals from foods. Categorisation by function or type is a major cognitive leap.

name: Sequence 3 Events
howTo: After a routine, ask what comes next: 'We had bath. Then what? Then what?' Three-event sequence recall is emerging.

name: Simple Puzzle 6–8 Pieces
howTo: 6–8 piece puzzle requiring rotation and trial-and-error. The frustration tolerance needed here is as developmental as the spatial skill.

name: Count 1–5 Objects
howTo: Place 3 objects in a line and count them together: touch each as you count. One-to-one correspondence beginning to appear.

name: Memory Card Match
howTo: 4 pairs of matching cards face-down. Turn over 2 at a time. Early working memory and concentration.

name: Emotion Management Practice
howTo: Before a frustrating task, name the strategy: 'If this is hard, take a breath.' Practice during calm so it is available during frustration.

name: Turn Taking in Games
howTo: Establish clear turn-taking in a simple game. 'Meri baari. Ab tumhari baari.' Consistent language makes the rule learnable.

name: Empathy Practice
howTo: Point out someone who is sad or hurt. 'Woh roh raha hai. Use dard hua. Hum kya kar sakte hain?' Empathy is taught through narration.

name: Pretend Play Social
howTo: Set up a tea party or cooking scenario with dolls. Taking roles in pretend play is social cognition and narrative combined.

name: Self-Advocacy Seed
howTo: When toddler is upset, model the phrase: 'I don't like that' or 'Mujhe yeh pasand nahi.' Give them words for their feelings.

name: Comfort Skill Building
howTo: Introduce a simple self-comfort strategy in a calm moment: slow breathing, squeezing a soft object. Practice before it is needed.

name: Water Transfer Play
howTo: Two containers of water, a cup for transferring. Supervised water play for 15 min. Pouring, splashing, and measuring emerge naturally.

name: Playdough Shapes
howTo: Roll, flatten, and cut playdough with a blunt knife. Making shapes adds visual-motor control to the tactile input.

name: Nature Scavenger Hunt
howTo: Walk outside and collect one of each: a leaf, a stone, a stick, a feather. Touch and describe each one together.

name: Bubble Play
howTo: Blow bubbles and let toddler pop them. Tracking, reaching, timing, and the satisfying pop make this multi-sensory and motivating.

name: Paint with Hands
howTo: Finger painting (food-safe paint or safe craft paint). Each colour is introduced separately. Direct contact with material.

name: Dressing Participation
howTo: Name each clothing item as it goes on. Ask toddler to help push arm through sleeve or lift foot for shoe. Participation builds independence.

name: Teeth Brushing Ritual
howTo: Brush teeth together at the same time. Letting toddler hold and attempt the brush first builds cooperation with the hygiene routine.

name: Running Obstacle Course
howTo: Set up household obstacles to run around: chairs, cushions, a line of tape. Navigating while running requires real-time motor planning.

name: Jump Over a Line
howTo: Put a tape line on the floor. Jump over with both feet. Clearing an obstacle while jumping = significantly harder than jumping in place.

name: Walk Backward
howTo: Practice walking backward, first holding hands then free. Backward locomotion requires body-awareness and spatial recalibration.

name: Throw and Catch (Large Ball)
howTo: Roll a large ball back and forth, then graduate to low throwing and catching. Catching a rolling ball before a thrown one.

name: Pedal a Tricycle
howTo: Practice on a tricycle or balance bike. Pedalling requires reciprocal leg movement — the same pattern as walking but with sustained force.

name: Gallop Forward
howTo: Demonstrate a gallop (lead-foot, drag) and encourage copying. Galloping before skipping — the intermediate coordination step.

name: Step Alternating Stairs (Up)
howTo: Encourage alternating feet on the way up the stairs. May still need rail; alternating feet up is a 24–30 month milestone.

name: Push and Pull Heavy Objects
howTo: Encourage pushing a chair or pulling a loaded bag. Resistance exercise builds core strength and spatial navigation simultaneously.

name: Copy Drawing: Horizontal Line
howTo: Show a horizontal line (left to right) and ask child to copy. Directionality in drawing precedes directionality in writing.

name: Copy Drawing: Circle
howTo: Demonstrate a circle slowly and let child try. Circle-copying typically appears 24–30 months — earlier than + or V shapes.

name: Snip with Scissors
howTo: Child-safe scissors: snip fringe into paper strips. Each snip is a complete bilateral motor action.

name: Pour from Jug to Cup
howTo: Pour water from a small jug into a cup. The control of flow is a daily self-care fine motor skill used for years.

name: Puzzle (8–10 Pieces)
howTo: 8–10 piece puzzle requiring rotation and spatial reasoning. Systematically trying each piece before accepting failure is the cognitive goal.

name: Sort Colours (3 Colours)
howTo: Sort household objects into 3 colour groups. Naming the colours correctly while sorting combines language and cognition.

name: 200+ Word Vocabulary
howTo: 200 words by 24 months is the benchmark (CDC). Under 50 words by 24 months is worth professional discussion.

name: Two- to Three-Word Phrases
howTo: Mama, more water please.' Three-word phrases mark a significant vocabulary and grammar step appearing 21–24 months.

name: Use 'I' and 'Me'
howTo: I want' and 'Give me' appearing means self-concept is strongly established. Model these forms throughout the day.

name: Ask Open Questions
howTo: What happened at the park today?' Not 'Did you have fun?' Open questions require memory, sequencing, and language simultaneously.

name: Story Prediction
howTo: During book reading, stop before a page turn: 'What do you think will happen next?' Prediction requires language plus narrative cognition.

name: Name Colours in Environment
howTo: Not a colour worksheet — just naming colours of real objects throughout the day. Context makes the association stronger.

name: Rhyming Play
howTo: Cat — bat — sat — mat!' Rhyming awareness at 24 months predicts reading readiness. Even partial awareness is worth celebrating.

name: Describe Daily Events
howTo: At bedtime, ask child to tell you two things that happened today. This builds narrative language and episodic memory together.

name: Sort by Size (Big/Small)
howTo: Sort objects into two groups: big and small. Size concept develops through sorting, not worksheets.

name: Sequence Daily Routine
howTo: Ask: 'What do we do after breakfast? Then what?' Three to four event sequence recall is the target at this age.

name: Complete a Simple Pattern
howTo: Build a simple colour or shape pattern: red, blue, red, blue — and leave a gap. Can child predict what comes next?

name: Concept: Full and Empty
howTo: Pour water into an empty glass; let child pour it back. 'Full. Empty. Full again.' Concrete object manipulation precedes abstract concept.

name: Match Photo to Person
howTo: Show baby photos of family members. Can child identify who it is? Memory across time = abstract object permanence.

name: Counting with One-to-One Correspondence
howTo: Place 4 objects in a line; touch each as you count 1-2-3-4. Guide child's hand to touch each. Counting with meaning, not reciting.

name: Sharing Practice (Guided)
howTo: During play: 'You have 4 blocks. Can you give me 2?' Guided sharing builds number concept alongside social skill.

name: Cooperative Building
howTo: Build something together: 'I put one block, you put one block.' Turn-taking in construction is cooperative play at its clearest.

name: Feelings Vocabulary (5 Emotions)
howTo: Name 5 emotions accurately this week: happy, sad, angry, scared, excited. Emotional vocabulary directly predicts social competence.

name: Pretend Play Elaboration
howTo: Join child's pretend play and add a new element: 'The baby is sleeping — shall we sing her a lori?' Extending the narrative.

name: Frustration Script
howTo: Teach a specific phrase for frustration: 'I need help' or 'Mujhe madad chahiye.' Practice during calm — not during the moment.

name: Apology Practice
howTo: When child hurts or upsets another: 'What could you say? How do you think they felt?' Modelling, not forcing. Empathy precedes apology.

name: Sensory Walk Barefoot
howTo: Walk barefoot on grass, sand, and smooth pavement on the same outing. Noticing the difference is the sensory lesson.

name: Mixing Colours (Water)
howTo: Add food colouring to water in clear cups and mix two together. Watching red + blue = purple is both science and sensory.

name: Musical Instruments Exploration
howTo: Pots, boxes, metal bowls — each makes a different sound. Let child experiment with what each material produces.

name: Clay (Atta) Detailed Work
howTo: Press small objects into dough to make impressions. Roll thin snakes. Cut with blunt knife. Precision work in tactile medium.
materials: Atta dough and objects to press

name: Weighted Blanket Cuddle
howTo: Wrap child in a heavy blanket on a lap. Deep pressure input is calming for the autonomic nervous system.

name: Independent Dressing (Simple)
howTo: By 24 months: pull trousers up and down, remove shoes and socks, help with shirts. All with support — independence is incremental.

name: Toilet Training Awareness
howTo: If interest appears: describe what toilet training involves. Let child see the process. No pressure — readiness signs should lead.

name: Jump Forward (Both Feet)
howTo: Encourage jumping forward from standing, landing on both feet. Distance of jump increases each week as leg strength grows.

name: Walk on a Balance Beam
howTo: A plank, a garden wall, or tape on the floor. Walk along without falling off. Balance on a narrow path is a 2.5-year skill.

name: Hop on One Foot (Attempt)
howTo: Hold child's hand and encourage hopping on one foot. Even one hop is the milestone beginning — don't expect sustained hopping yet.

name: Catch a Bounced Ball
howTo: Bounce a large ball to child. Catching a bounced ball before a thrown one — the visual tracking time is longer.

name: Pedal with Steering
howTo: Tricycle: practice steering around objects. Combining pedalling with directional control is a significant motor coordination step.

name: Animal Movement Play
howTo: Move like different animals: frog jump, bear walk, crab walk, snake slither. Each uses different muscle groups and movement patterns.

name: Throw Overhand
howTo: Demonstrate an overhand throw and let child try. Overhand requires trunk rotation — a very different movement than underhand.

name: Summersault (Assisted)
howTo: Help child do a forward roll on a soft surface. Head tuck, push-off, and landing = vestibular, motor, and spatial all together.

name: Copy Drawing: Plus Sign (+)
howTo: Show a + (cross) and let child try. Requires two directional lines crossing — harder than circle; appears around 30–36 months.

name: Use Fork Independently
howTo: Fork for stabbing soft foods. The grip and stabbing force are different from a spoon — a distinct fine motor skill.

name: Dress a Doll
howTo: Button, zip, and dress a doll. This is fine motor practice that feels purposeful and maintains engagement longer.

name: Fold Paper in Half
howTo: Show folding a piece of paper in half and ask child to try. Aligning edges before folding requires spatial and motor precision.

name: Sort by 2 Attributes
howTo: Sort blocks by BOTH colour AND size together. Multi-attribute sorting is more demanding than single-attribute.
materials: Blocks in multiple colours and sizes

name: Lace a Pattern Board
howTo: Lace thread through holes to form a simple picture. Requires planning the sequence of holes to achieve the intended shape.

name: Tell a Simple Story
howTo: Ask child to tell a story about an animal they know. Even 2–3 sentences with a character is the emergence of narrative.

name: Ask and Answer Questions
howTo: Why does it rain?' 'What would happen if…?' Complex question forms are emerging — answer simply and turn it back.

name: Three- to Four-Word Sentences
howTo: Consistent 3–4 word sentences with grammar: 'I want the red ball.' Grammar errors ('I goed') are developmentally correct now.

name: Rhyming Detection
howTo: Does cat rhyme with bat? What about cat and dog?' Detecting rhyme before producing it — typical at 25–30 months.

name: Describe a Picture
howTo: Show a picture and ask 'What is happening here?' Child describes scene — vocabulary, grammar, and observation all combined.

name: First and Last Name
howTo: Practice saying full name. 'What is your full name?' is a social comprehension milestone by age 3.

name: Conversation with Questions
howTo: Have a 5-turn conversation where child asks at least one question. Asking is more advanced than answering.

name: Story from Memory
howTo: After reading a favourite book many times, ask child to 'read' it to you from the pictures. Memory narrative is emerging.

name: Count Objects to 5
howTo: Place up to 5 objects in a line and count together, touching each one. One-to-one correspondence solidifying now.

name: Basic Opposites
howTo: Big/small, hot/cold, fast/slow, loud/quiet. Opposites build comparative conceptual thinking.

name: Yesterday and Today
howTo: Yesterday we went to the park. Today we are home.' Time concepts past/present solidify through consistent narration.

name: Sort 4 Categories
howTo: Sort objects into 4 groups: food, animals, clothes, vehicles. Four-category sorting is sophisticated categorical thinking.

name: Pattern Extension (ABAB)
howTo: Build red-blue-red-blue and leave a gap: 'What comes next?' Pattern extension requires holding the rule in working memory.

name: Simple Addition Concept
howTo: Here are 2 bananas. I add 1 more. How many now?' Concrete addition before abstract number.

name: Imaginary Friend Engagement
howTo: If an imaginary friend appears, engage with them: 'What is their name?' Imaginary companions support language, emotional, and social development.

name: Negotiate a Trade
howTo: When a conflict arises over a toy: 'What could you offer them to trade?' Negotiation is a social skill that must be taught explicitly.

name: Brag Board
howTo: Create a display of child's achievements (drawings, photos). 'You did all of these!' Pride in accomplishment is a social-emotional milestone.

name: Role Play (Doctor, Chef)
howTo: Set up a role-play scenario with simple props. Role-play at 25–30 months involves taking on another's perspective.

name: Regulation Practice: Pause
howTo: When feelings escalate, say 'Let's take a pause' and model slow breathing together. Practice before it is needed.

name: Ask How Others Feel
howTo: While reading or in real life: 'How do you think she felt when that happened?' Perspective-taking practice.

name: Sensory Art: Tissue Paper Collage
howTo: Tear and paste coloured tissue paper onto card. Tearing texture, paper texture, and glue texture are layered sensory inputs.

name: Outdoor Water Play
howTo: Watering can, puddles, or garden tap. Child-directed water exploration is rich sensory and cause-effect play.

name: Texture Sorting Game
howTo: Gather 8 objects of varied texture. Sort into 'rough' and 'smooth.' Tactile discrimination is now a language + sensory task.

name: Proprioceptive Heavy Work
howTo: Carrying loaded backpack, pushing a box of books, pulling a weighted trolley. Heavy work regulates the nervous system.

name: Spin on Spot
howTo: Spin with arms out, stop, try to stay balanced. Vestibular system input — intentional dizziness and recovery is regulating.

name: Brush Teeth Independently (Attempt)
howTo: Let child brush their own teeth first, then parent finishes. Agency in the sequence builds cooperation with the hygiene routine.

name: Toilet Training (If Ready)
howTo: If signs of readiness present (knowing when wet, interest in toilet), begin with simple potty introduction. Never forced.

name: Hop on One Foot (3–5 Hops)
howTo: From one hop, build to 3–5 consecutive hops on the same foot. Each hop requires rebalancing — rapid balance adjustment developing.

name: Skip (Gallop to Skip)
howTo: Most children gallop at 2.5 years and skip at 3.5. Practice gallop leading with each foot as the precursor.

name: Catch a Thrown Ball
howTo: Graduate from bounced to thrown ball catching. Tracking the trajectory and adjusting arms = complex visual-motor planning.

name: Pedal and Brake
howTo: On a tricycle: practice pedalling and stopping at a marked line. Braking intentionally requires coordinated leg action.

name: Climb Ladder (Playground)
howTo: Climbing a ladder — alternating hands and feet — is the most complex locomotion pattern children this age attempt.

name: Jump from Height (30 cm)
howTo: Jump off a 30-cm step with both feet landing together. Judging safe heights and landing = spatial and motor cognition combined.

name: Balance Beam (Eyes Closed)
howTo: Walk a balance beam (tape line) with eyes closed for 2 steps. Eyes-closed balance challenges proprioceptive system intensely.

name: Dodge and Weave Game
howTo: Chase game where child must dodge around obstacles. Reactive motor planning — responding to unexpected changes in a path.

name: Copy Drawing: V Shape
howTo: Show a V and ask child to copy. Angular shapes (V, then +, then triangle) appear in sequence after circle.

name: Draw a Person (Head + 2 Parts)
howTo: Ask child to draw a person. Head + one other body part by 30 months = fine motor and representational thinking combined.

name: Scissors in a Straight Line
howTo: Cut along a straight line drawn on paper. Staying on the line requires visual monitoring while maintaining bilateral grip.

name: Peel and Stick Labels
howTo: Peel self-adhesive stickers and place on a target. Two-stage finger action requiring precise coordination.

name: Build a Bridge (3 Blocks)
howTo: Demonstrate placing a block across two towers and ask child to build the same. Copying spatial models = architecture thinking.

name: String Small Beads
howTo: Small beads on a thin lace. Fine pincer control plus visual targeting plus threading = high-demand fine motor task.

name: 500+ Word Vocabulary
howTo: A 30-month-old typically has 450–600 words. Importantly, sentences are 3–5 words with mostly correct grammar.

name: Tell Stories with Beginning-Middle-End
howTo: Once there was a dog. He was hungry. He found some food and ate it.' Three-part narrative structure is the target.

name: Because' and 'If' Sentences
howTo: I'm tired because I didn't sleep.' 'If it rains, we'll stay inside.' Logical connectors mark a grammar milestone.

name: Describe How Something Works
howTo: How does a tap work?' Let child explain from their own understanding. Explanatory language is emerging.

name: Rhyme Production
howTo: I say cat — you say something that rhymes.' Production (not just detection) of rhymes = phonological awareness step.

name: Letter Name Recognition (Own Name)
howTo: Recognise the first letter of own name in print. This is enough letter knowledge to celebrate at 30 months.
materials: Paper with child's name in large letters

name: Complex Question Response
howTo: What would you do if it was raining and you wanted to go outside?' Hypothetical thinking + language combined.

name: Storytelling from Memory
howTo: Retell a favourite story from memory using the book's pictures as prompts. 3-event sequence is the typical recall at this age.

name: Count to 10 with Meaning
howTo: Count 10 objects touching each one. At 30 months, 10-object counting with one-to-one correspondence is an achievable goal.

name: Concept: Same and Different
howTo: Are these the same or different?' — with objects that are clearly one or the other. Comparative language + cognition.
materials: Pairs of matching and non-matching objects

name: Categorise by Function
howTo: Group things that you eat, things you wear, things you sit on. Sorting by function is more abstract than sorting by appearance.

name: Spatial Concepts: In, On, Under, Behind
howTo: Put the cup on the book. Now under the book.' Following spatial prepositions in sequence.

name: Day Sequence: Morning, Afternoon, Evening
howTo: What do we do in the morning? What happens in the evening?' Time-of-day sequencing before days of the week.

name: Simple Inference
howTo: While reading: 'Why is the bear sad?' — answer not in the text but inferrable from pictures. Early inferential thinking.

name: Play in Small Group (3 Children)
howTo: Facilitate play in a group of 3. Children this age can begin brief cooperative interaction — note who initiates and who follows.

name: Express Feelings With Words
howTo: Mujhe gussa aa raha hai' or 'I feel scared.' Verbal emotion expression before or instead of physical expression.

name: Help a Younger Child
howTo: When a younger child needs help with something child can do: 'Can you show them how to stack the blocks?' Pro-social seed.

name: Choose an Activity
howTo: Offer 3 activities and let child choose. 'What would you like to do first?' Autonomous choice builds decision-making.

name: Deal with Disappointment Script
howTo: When something doesn't happen as planned, narrate: 'You're disappointed. That was important to you. Let's think about what we can do.'

name: Fairness Conversations
howTo: Is it fair that she got 3 and you got 2?' Fairness reasoning appears at 2.5 years and is important to take seriously.

name: Cornstarch Goop (Oobleck)
howTo: Mix cornstarch and water — it's both solid and liquid. Scientifically bizarre sensory experience. Let child explore freely.

name: Sound Walk
howTo: Walk outside listening only — no talking. Point at sounds. Back home, draw or describe what you heard. Auditory attention focus.

name: Temperature Sensory Bin
howTo: Ice cubes in a bin of warm water. Feeling both together, watching ice melt. Temperature + observation + language.

name: Yoga for Kids (3 Poses)
howTo: Teach 3 simple yoga poses: tree, mountain, downward dog. Proprioceptive + balance + breath awareness combined.

name: Spin Top or Gyroscope
howTo: Let child spin a top and watch. The visual tracking of a spinning object is uniquely absorbing at this age.

name: Pour Own Drink (Jug)
howTo: Pour their own water from a small child-sized jug into a cup at meals. Independence in self-care + fine motor + self-regulation.

name: Help Set the Table
howTo: Carry plates, fold napkins, place cutlery. Table-setting is fine motor + sequencing + contribution to family life.

name: Hop 5+ Times (One Foot)
howTo: Sustained hopping on one foot — first dominant then non-dominant. Non-dominant hopping develops several months after dominant.

name: Broad Jump (Forward)
howTo: Mark a starting line with tape. Jump forward as far as possible, both feet together. Measure distance — it increases weekly.

name: Throw at a Vertical Target
howTo: Tape a target circle on the wall at chest height. Throw a soft ball to hit it. Aimed at a vertical target = new motor challenge.

name: Ride Tricycle Fast and Slow
howTo: Pedal fast when you say go, slow when you say stop. Speed regulation while pedalling requires real-time motor control.

name: Walk Backward on Balance Beam
howTo: Backward walking on a balance beam (tape line) — balance plus motor sequencing in an unusual direction.

name: Obstacle Course Run
howTo: A full obstacle course: run, jump over, crawl under, balance on, throw at. Complex movement sequence requiring memory of order.

name: Throw and Run Combination
howTo: Throw a ball, run to get it, throw again. Sequencing two motor actions with a transition tests motor working memory.

name: Marching in Place
howTo: Lift knees high and march in time to music. Rhythmic bilateral motor coordination and gross motor control.

name: Copy Drawing: Square
howTo: Square (4 equal sides, 4 corners) is harder than a circle — requires direction changes at precise points. Appears ~33–36 months.

name: Draw a Person (Head + 4 Parts)
howTo: Head, eyes, arms, legs. Drawing a person with 4 identifiable features is a 3-year representational drawing milestone.

name: Cut a Curved Line
howTo: After mastering straight-line cutting, introduce a curve to cut along. Following a curve requires continuous adjustment.

name: Button Large Buttons
howTo: Demonstrate and let child practice buttoning a shirt or coat with large buttons. Fine pincer + hand-eye coordination.
materials: Shirt or coat with large buttons

name: Weave Paper Strips
howTo: Weave paper strips over and under to make a simple mat. The alternating pattern requires sustained visual-motor tracking.

name: Trace Letters (Own Name)
howTo: Trace the letters of own name with a finger, then crayon. Letter tracing before writing = spatial learning of letter forms.

name: 700–900 Word Vocabulary
howTo: By 33 months, vocabulary typically 700–900 words with 5–6 word sentences used consistently.

name: Why' Conversation Chain
howTo: Follow a chain of 'why' questions: 'Why does it rain?' → 'Because the clouds get heavy.' → 'Why do they get heavy?' Sustain 3 turns.

name: Name All Basic Colours
howTo: Red, blue, green, yellow, orange, purple, black, white. Naming all basic colours correctly is a 3-year language milestone.

name: Use Plurals Correctly
howTo: Two dogs, three cats.' Plural '-s' rule solidifying. Point out examples: 'Look — two birds. Birds — more than one.'

name: Past Tense Regular Verbs
howTo: I walked. We played. She jumped.' Regular past tense (-ed) appearing. Irregular past ('went', 'ran') still developing.

name: Describe What You See
howTo: Tell me everything you see in this picture.' Descriptive language drill — vocabulary, grammar, and observation combined.

name: Conditional Sentences
howTo: If we water the plant, it will grow.' If-then reasoning expressed in language — logical thinking made verbal.

name: Letter Sound Introduction (3 Letters)
howTo: Introduce 3 letter sounds: 'A says ah, B says bah, M says mah.' Sound-letter pairs before letter names — phonics groundwork.

name: Count to 15 with Meaning
howTo: Extend counting to 15 objects with one-to-one correspondence. Counting past 10 requires learning the teen number pattern.

name: Name All Basic Shapes
howTo: Circle, square, triangle, rectangle, oval. Naming all 5 basic shapes by name = geometry milestone at 33 months.

name: More and Fewer
howTo: Place 3 objects here and 5 there. 'Which group has more?' Comparative quantity — not counting, but visual quantity judgement.

name: Memory Game (6 Pairs)
howTo: 6 matching pairs face-down. Turn 2, find matches. Working memory and concentration targeted directly.

name: Sequence a Story (4 Pictures)
howTo: 4 story pictures out of order. Can child arrange them in logical sequence? Narrative + causal reasoning combined.

name: Concept: First, Middle, Last
howTo: Line up 3 objects. 'Which is first? Last? Middle?' Ordinal position language builds mathematical foundation.

name: Friend Concept
howTo: Who is your friend? What do you like about them?' Friendship awareness at 31–33 months is a social milestone.

name: Take Turns in Group Game
howTo: Play a group game with 3–4 children where turns rotate. Supporting turn-taking in a group is more complex than in a pair.

name: Accepting 'No' Practice
howTo: When a request must be declined, practice accepting it with words: 'Okay, maybe later.' Delayed gratification is teachable.

name: Cooperative Drawing
howTo: Two people draw on the same paper at the same time. Sharing a creative space without conflict is social maturity.
materials: Large paper and crayons for two

name: Identify Emotions in Others (Real Life)
howTo: Dadi looks tired today. What do you think she needs?' Reading real (not illustrated) emotional states is a harder skill.

name: Comfort Peer in Distress
howTo: When another child is upset: 'Can you think of something that might help them feel better?' Pro-social action seeded.

name: Mud Kitchen Play
howTo: Outdoors: soil, water, pots, spoons. Make 'food', serve it, clean up. Sensory + imaginative + gross + fine motor all together.

name: Shadow Play
howTo: In bright sunlight, make and change shadow shapes. Tracing shadows on paper. Visual perception + fine motor + science.

name: Magnet Exploration
howTo: A magnet and various household objects. Which ones stick? Systematic testing of a material property.

name: Rhythm Clapping Patterns
howTo: Clap a 3-beat pattern and ask child to copy. Grade to 4-beat. Rhythmic working memory and motor sequencing.

name: Blindfold Texture Guess
howTo: Blindfold or closed eyes; feel an object and name it. Tactile recognition without visual aid.

name: Help Prepare a Simple Snack
howTo: Peel a banana, spread butter on toast, pour cereal. Contributing to own food preparation builds self-care and agency.

name: Dress Independently (Simple Items)
howTo: By 33 months: pull trousers up/down, put on shoes (even wrong feet), put on hat, take off jacket. Independence in sequence.

name: Skip (Alternating Feet)
howTo: True skipping — step-hop alternating feet — typically appears 3.5–4 years. Practice the step-hop on each foot separately first.

name: Throw and Catch (Tennis Ball)
howTo: Tennis-ball-sized throw and catch at 2 metres. Smaller ball demands greater precision than large-ball catching.

name: Hop 10+ Times
howTo: 10+ consecutive hops on the preferred foot. Non-preferred foot at this stage is typically 5–8 hops.

name: Broad Jump Over Line
howTo: Mark two lines 40 cm apart. Jump from one to the other with both feet. Distance increases as leg strength and timing improve.

name: Balance on One Foot (5 Seconds)
howTo: 5-second one-foot balance without support. Practice eyes open then eventually eyes closed.

name: Dribble a Ball (Bouncing)
howTo: Bounce and catch a ball repeatedly. Dribbling (bouncing without catching) is harder and typically 4–5 years.

name: Move to Music (Rhythm)
howTo: Move to the beat of different musical styles. Rhythmic entrainment — body movement matching musical tempo — is a motor milestone.

name: Gallop with Object in Hand
howTo: Gallop while holding an object in one hand. Dual-task motor automatisation: galloping becomes automatic enough for a second task.

name: Copy Drawing: Triangle
howTo: Triangle requires three directional line changes at precise angles. Typically appearing 36 months — harder than square.

name: Draw a Person (6 Parts)
howTo: Head, body, 2 arms, 2 legs. By 36 months: 6-part person is the benchmark drawing milestone.

name: Copy First Name (Tracing)
howTo: Trace each letter of first name carefully. Letter-form learning happens through the motor movement, not just visual recognition.

name: Use Child Scissors for Shape
howTo: Cut out a simple shape (circle or triangle) drawn on paper. Following curved and angular lines in cutting.

name: Fold Paper into Envelope
howTo: Fold a piece of paper in thirds and tuck in the edges to make a simple envelope. Spatial folding and precise crease-making.

name: Build Complex Block Structures
howTo: Build a house, bridge, or tower using a picture as a model. Copying a 3D structure from a 2D picture is abstract spatial cognition.

name: 1000+ Word Vocabulary
howTo: At 36 months, vocabulary typically 900–1200 words. Strangers should understand 75–100% of speech by this age.

name: Retell a Story (Sequence)
howTo: After reading a book, ask child to retell it in order without pictures. 4-event sequence recall is the 3-year target.

name: Use Past and Future Tense
howTo: Yesterday I played. Tomorrow we will go.' Past and future tense correct usage is a 3-year grammar milestone.

name: Explain How Something Works
howTo: Why does the ball roll? Why does the fan spin?' 3-year-olds begin to explain mechanisms, not just name them.

name: Letter Sound Game (5 Letters)
howTo: What sound does S make? Dog starts with what letter?' 5-letter sound associations by 36 months = strong phonics foundation.

name: 5-Word Sentences (Complex)
howTo: The big red dog ran away.' Complex sentences with adjectives and adverbs consistently = strong language development.

name: Debate: Why is X Better?
howTo: Is a cat or a dog better to have? Why?' Opinion + justification: the beginning of argument and persuasive language.

name: Rhyme a Word Family
howTo: Cat, bat, sat, hat, rat — all rhyme. What else rhymes with cat?' Generating rhymes from a family = phonological fluency.

name: Count to 20
howTo: Count 20 objects one-to-one. Past 12, children must remember the teen pattern; past 20, the decade pattern begins.

name: Concept of Zero
howTo: How many elephants are on this table? Zero. Zero means none.' Zero as a quantity is an abstract concept to teach explicitly.

name: Name 10 Colours
howTo: Red, blue, green, yellow, orange, purple, pink, black, white, brown. Naming all 10 basic colours by 36 months is solid.

name: Days of the Week Introduction
howTo: Sing or say days of the week in sequence. Memorising the sequence before understanding the concept — sequence comes first.

name: Pattern Prediction (AABB)
howTo: AABB pattern: red, red, blue, blue, red, red… 'What comes next?' Two-repeat pattern is harder than ABAB.

name: Cause-Effect Explanation
howTo: Why did that happen? What caused it?' Causal explanation — not just observation but mechanism — is a 3-year cognitive goal.

name: Cooperative Game (Rules)
howTo: Play a simple game with explicit rules (ludo, snap). Following rules in a game is the first social contract — a major SE milestone.

name: Conflict Resolution Script
howTo: Teach: 'Stop. Think. Speak.' When a conflict happens, model the steps: pause, consider the other person, use words.

name: Recognise Own Feelings Early
howTo: I notice your face looks cross. Are you feeling frustrated before it comes out big?' Self-awareness before dysregulation.

name: Apology with Empathy
howTo: I'm sorry I took your toy. I know that made you sad.' Empathy embedded in apology: what they did + how the other felt.

name: Winning and Losing Gracefully
howTo: Practice in a real game. Celebrate both: 'You lost this time and stayed kind. That is very hard and very mature.'

name: Best-Friend Identification
howTo: Who is your favourite person to play with? What do you do together?' Intentional friendship at 3 is a social milestone.

name: Resist-and-Wait Practice
howTo: I know you want it now. Let's wait 2 minutes together.' Practise with a timer. Delayed gratification is a teachable executive function.

name: Slime Making
howTo: Mix glue and bicarbonate of soda (or contact lens solution). Unique tactile input — stretchy, gooey, satisfying. Full sensory engagement.
materials: PVA glue, bicarbonate of soda, contact lens solution

name: Sensory Story Walk
howTo: Walk a route where child closes eyes at each stop and describes what they hear and feel. One sense at a time, deliberately.

name: Nature Printing
howTo: Press leaves, bark, or flowers with paint onto paper. The texture transfer is visual, tactile, and creative simultaneously.

name: Blindfold Object Guess
howTo: Feel objects in a bag without looking. Name or describe them. Pure tactile recognition with language challenge added.

name: Rhythm Band
howTo: Assign different percussion sounds to different family members. Create a rhythm piece together. Auditory + motor + social.

name: Simple Self-Care Sequence (Morning)
howTo: Wake, toilet, wash face, brush teeth, dress — child does as much as possible. Independence in sequence, not perfection in execution.

name: Help with Household Chores
howTo: Set the table, put laundry in the basket, water a plant. Contributing to household function builds competence and belonging.

name: Skip Distance Challenge
